proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Writing the orbit of u_j as {u_{j1}, ..., u_{jn_j}}, take the pair W' inside W inside U of the finite-flat-over-almost-dense lemma. Since U = t(s^{-1} of the closure of W), some u_{ji} lies in the closure of W; as a generic point of an irreducible component of a locally Noetherian scheme it lies in W itself; by R-invariance of W the whole orbit of u_j lies in W. By the cohomology-of-schemes lemma on images of finite morphisms over affine bases in the Noetherian setting, it suffices to find an R-invariant affine open V' of W' containing u_1, ..., u_m, because the corresponding open V of W will be affine; hence replace (U, R, s, t, c) by the restriction to W', where s and t are finite locally free. By the properties maximal-points lemma one finds an affine open containing all orbit points (a locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated by the locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated lemma), and the groupoids find-invariant-affine lemma concludes. (source lines 2859-2884)

core_obligations: Orbit containment: let {u_{j1}, ..., u_{jn_j}} be the orbit of u_j and take W' inside W from lemma-finite-flat-over-almost-dense-subscheme; its covering U = t(s^{-1}(W closure)) puts at least one u_{ji} in the closure of W; generic point of an irreducible component plus locally Noetherian implies u_{ji} in W; R-invariance of W gives u_j in W and the whole orbit in W (proof lines 2860-2867). Reduction: by coherent-lemma-image-affine-finite-morphism-affine-Noetherian it suffices to find an R-invariant affine open V' of W' containing u_1, ..., u_m, taking V inside W to be the corresponding open (affine because the thickening is finite); replace the groupoid by its restriction to W', where s and t are finite locally free (proof lines 2868-2876). Conclusion: properties-lemma-maximal-points-affine gives an affine open containing all the orbit points, the locally Noetherian scheme being quasi-separated by properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated; applying groupoids-lemma-find-invariant-affine to this data produces the R-invariant affine open and finishes the proof (proof lines 2877-2883).
proof_roadmap: Use the almost-dense pair and the covering property to pull the orbits into W (proof lines 2860-2867).
Reduce to the finite locally free restriction W' via the affine-image criterion for finite morphisms (proof lines 2868-2876).
Find an affine open around the finitely many orbit points (maximal-points lemma with quasi-separatedness), then apply the groupoids find-invariant-affine lemma (proof lines 2877-2883).
